title: Check if Strings Can be Made Equal With Operations II
spaceBreakdown:
- cnt1[2][26]: 52 integers, constant size → O(1)
- cnt2[2][26]: 52 integers, constant size → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input strings s1, s2
approach: The operation allows swapping any two positions with the same parity (since j−i is even ⟺ i and j share the same parity). This means characters at even indices can be freely rearranged among even indices, and characters at odd indices among odd indices. Therefore, s1 and s2 can be made equal if and only if the multiset of characters at even positions in s1 equals that in s2, and the same holds for odd positions. We use frequency arrays of size 26 for each parity group to compare in O(n) time.
hints: When j − i is even, what must be true about the parities of i and j? The constraint n ≤ 10^5 rules out simulating every possible sequence of swaps.

Use frequency arrays indexed by character, separated into two groups by index parity. For s1 = "abcdba", even-indexed characters are {a, c, b} and odd-indexed are {b, d, a}; build the same groups for s2 and compare.

**Two characters, different parities** - indices 0 and 1 differ by 1 (odd), so no swap is allowed.
`Input: s1 = "ab", s2 = "ba"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: comparing only total character frequency across all positions → returns true

**Equal multisets, different order within parity** - same characters at each parity but in different order.
`Input: s1 = "cba", s2 = "abc"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: comparing parity groups as raw strings without sorting or counting → returns false

**Single character mismatch** - only index 0 exists, no swaps possible.
`Input: s1 = "a", s2 = "b"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true whenever the two strings have equal length → returns true

**Same total counts, wrong parity distribution** - total character counts match but parity groups differ.
`Input: s1 = "abcd", s2 = "badc"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only total character counts across all positions → returns true

followUps.q: What if the operation allowed any swap (j − i can be odd or even)?
followUps.a: Characters could move freely to any position, so we would only need the total multiset of characters to match. Use a single frequency array of size 26 per string and compare. O(n) time, O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if you can only swap positions where j − i = 2 (adjacent same-parity positions only)?
followUps.a: Within each parity group, only adjacent swaps are allowed, so we need to count inversions between s1 and s2's parity subsequence to find the minimum swaps required. O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

followUps.q: What if the strings arrive as a stream and are too large to store in memory?
followUps.a: Process characters one at a time, maintaining four frequency arrays of size 26 (even/odd for each string). Each incoming character increments one counter. Compare all 52 counters at the end. O(n) time, O(1) space (104 integers total).
